Definition: from G3432; (middle voice) to commit adultery:--commit adultery.
BiblicalUsage: Moichao is the middle-voice form of committing adultery — whoever puts away his wife and marries another commits adultery, and so does the man who marries her that is put away. In the Greek text these middle forms stand under the lemma μοιχάομαι, spelled differently from this study's headword.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus draws the line where the heart draws it: adultery is not only the act, it is the breaking of the bond.
